title: Clustered Columnstore Index for Analytics
description: Create a clustered columnstore index to optimize analytical queries on a large fact table.

data.text: You have a large `SalesFact` table with millions of rows used for analytical queries (SUM, AVG, GROUP BY). Create a clustered columnstore index to optimize it.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
-- Drop existing clustered index (if any)
-- DROP INDEX IX_SalesFact_Clustered ON SalesFact;

-- Create clustered columnstore index
CREATE CLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE INDEX IX_SalesFact_Columnstore
ON SalesFact;

-- Add a nonclustered index for point lookups if needed:
-- CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_SalesFact_OrderID
-- ON SalesFact (OrderID)
-- INCLUDE (ProductID, Quantity, SalesAmount, OrderDate);

-- Query pattern that benefits:
SELECT
    YEAR(OrderDate) AS Year,
    ProductID,
    SUM(SalesAmount) AS TotalSales,
    AVG(Quantity) AS AvgQuantity,
    COUNT(*) AS TransactionCount
FROM SalesFact
GROUP BY YEAR(OrderDate), ProductID
ORDER BY Year, ProductID;

data.title: Explanation
data.text: Columnstore indexes store data column-by-column rather than row-by-row, offering 10x–100x compression and faster aggregation queries. A clustered columnstore index IS the table storage. Add nonclustered indexes on top for point lookups (ORDER BY specific OrderID). Best for data warehousing/analytics workloads.
